reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in treating video reasoning as an agent-driven process where each step involves deliberation followed by selective data retrieval. This dual-mode operation—thought followed by tool use—enables deep reasoning over temporal sequences. The trajectory optimization framework defines a sequence of observations, thoughts, and actions, which are evaluated using a reward mechanism that encourages effective tool usage. The gated reward design ensures that rewards are only given when tool usage contributes meaningfully to accuracy, preventing unnecessary computation. By incorporating a curiosity bonus, the system also promotes exploratory behavior within bounds. In GSE context, this translates into a policy engine that dynamically decides whether to invoke low-cost or high-cost video-processing modules based on confidence thresholds and expected utility. The cost-accuracy tradeoff further refines this by penalizing redundant or inefficient tool usage, aligning with computational budgets. These primitives form a coherent foundation for autonomous, adaptive video reasoning systems capable of multi-sport, multi-task analysis.
